message.content:
Fix three small defects in michi-pipeline before the 0.11.0 release. Repo: orin-dx/michi. Start your branch from `origin/main` (commit 92c611e3 or later); name it `fix/pipeline-start-record`. Read AGENTS.md first (rules: prefix shell commands with `rtk`; tests via `cargo nextest run`; no unwrap/expect in lib code; comments wrap at 120 cols, plain language; every claim needs a test that fails when broken — verify by introducing a mutant, watching the test fail, reverting).

Defects (found by review of main; verify each against the code first):
1. `crates/michi-pipeline/src/scheduler.rs` ~:430 and the early returns ~:692-703. After the change that moved `DurableObserver::record_start` onto a blocking thread, a step can end `Skipped(Cancelled)` or `Failed` with `DeadlinePassed` in the post-save re-check without ever being invoked, yet the record still gets `started_at` and `elapsed` (elapsed = the save's duration). Only `NotRun(StartNotRecorded)` currently skips them. Fix: a step that was never invoked records no `started_at`/`elapsed`. Add tests (durable run with a slow `record_start` + cancel during the save; and a deadline window ending during the save) asserting `started_at` is None.
2. Same file: the post-save deadline check (~:696) writes a different message ("the window of deadline group K ended…") than `deadline_passed` (~:353-356, "the {n}ms window of deadline group K…") for the same event. Make both use one helper/one message. Test the message equality across both paths if practical.
3. The `DurableObserver::record_start` doc (crates/michi-pipeline/src/exec.rs ~:91) implies a slow save does not delay cancellation. `spawn_blocking` can't be aborted and `drive` waits for the JoinSet, so a hung `record_start` keeps `execute` from returning even after cancel. Correct the doc to say so plainly.

Also add one changeset file `.changeset/pipeline-start-record.md` with front matter `michi-pipeline: patch` describing the user-visible fix in 1-3 plain sentences (follow the style of the existing files in .changeset/).

Verify: `cargo nextest run -p michi-pipeline`, `cargo clippy -p michi-pipeline --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `just fmt-check` (or `cargo fmt --check`). Judge by exit code. Commit with a conventional message (`fix(pipeline): ...`), no session links or Claude-Session trailers in the message. Push the branch to origin (normal push, never force, never to main). Do NOT open a PR. Report: branch name, commit sha, what changed, test names added, mutant results, and the exit codes of each check.

The closure gets an owned `StepContext`, and its result is the attempt's result. A panic in it ends the step `Panicked`.
docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:125:- **`JoinSet` drop.** Each attempt runs inside the scheduler's `JoinSet`. Dropping the `execute` or `resume` future aborts the async side, but Tokio never aborts a `spawn_blocking` task, so the closure runs to completion and its result is discarded. The closure's token fires, so a closure that watches it can stop early. The runtime waits for blocking threads when it shuts down.
docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md:360:- With it, `record_start` is called instead of `on_step_started`, before the step's first attempt, on a blocking thread (`spawn_blocking`) owned by that step's task. Steps that start together save their markers concurrently and in no fixed order, so `record_start` must be safe to call concurrently; a slow save delays only its own step (see "Durable starts run off the scheduler task" in `06-decisions.md`). `Ok` runs the step. `Err(reason)` or a panic does not: the step ends `NotRun(StartNotRecorded)` with the reason, its dependents are skipped, other branches carry on (fail-fast stops the run, as for any failure), and a panic is counted in `observer_panics()`. Nothing was invoked, so resume runs it again. The save can take a while, so the step looks again once it returns: if the run was cancelled meanwhile (by the caller or by fail-fast) the step ends `Skipped(Cancelled)`, and if its deadline group's window ended meanwhile it ends `Failed` with `DeadlinePassed`. Either way `Step::run` is not called, as if the change had landed just before dispatch.
crates/michi-pipeline/README.md:116:`step_blocking` runs a synchronous closure on Tokio's blocking thread pool, for steps that shell out to `cargo`, `npm` or `twine`. A blocking closure can't be stopped from outside: after a timeout or cancellation the executor stops waiting, but the closure keeps running, so it should watch `ctx.cancellation()`, which fires then, and kill any child process it started. A non-idempotent blocking step never starts a second closure while an earlier one with the same idempotency key (the same step in the same run) is still running.
